exposure: Perception of unlikely immediate post-birth problems
Perceived understanding of medical complication risks
outcome: Utilization of postnatal care services within the first 48 hours after birth
cohort: The study included 90 mothers of newborns aged 0-6 months, residing in conflict-affected urban and rural areas of northwest Syria, categorized by their attendance (DOERS) or non-attendance (NON-DOERS) of postnatal care within 48 hours of birth.
finding: The study identified significant barriers such as long distance to health facilities, social norms, and fear of COVID-19, as well as enablers like community health worker support and maternal education, that influenced the utilization of postnatal care services within 48 hours of birth.
mod_finding: Among the interviewed mothers, 68% had a normal delivery at health facilities, 20% had a cesarean delivery, and 12% had a normal delivery at home.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from 7th to 11th November 2021, among mothers of newborns aged 0-6 months.
